# Meta Workbench

> Free tools for meta-analysis and systematic review, built by R. Dong,
> a physician and systematic reviewer. Every tool runs entirely in your
> browser: no sign-up, no uploads, no watermarks, no fees.
> Homepage: https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/

## Tools

- [PRISMA Flow Diagram Generator](https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/prisma-flow-diagram-generator/):
  Enter identification, screening and inclusion counts and download a
  publication-ready PRISMA 2020 flow diagram as PNG. Counts are
  cross-checked automatically. One included study can have several reports.

- [Forest Plot Generator](https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/forest-plot-generator/):
  Paste study-level effect estimates and 95% CIs and get a forest plot with
  fixed-effect and DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooling, I-squared and
  tau-squared. Pooling code validated against an independent Python
  calculation. Download as PNG, no watermark.

- [RoB 2 Traffic-Light Plot Generator](https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/rob-traffic-light-generator/):
  Turn per-domain risk-of-bias judgements into the traffic-light and summary
  plots journals expect. Overall judgements follow the RoB 2 rule
  (Low / Some concerns / High); summary bars can be weighted by sample size.
  No R or robvis needed. The tool only draws the plots; judgements come from
  your own RoB 2 assessments.

- [Sample Size Calculator](https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/sample-size-calculator/):
  Two independent means, two independent proportions, and non-inferiority
  designs, with the formula shown and an attrition adjustment
  (recruitment target inflated as n / (1 - attrition)). Not for paired,
  survival or cluster designs.

## Common questions

- Is this free? Yes, all four tools are free, with no account and no
  installation.
- Is my data uploaded anywhere? No. Everything runs locally in your browser;
  nothing leaves your computer.
- Can I use the downloaded figures in a journal submission? Yes, PNG
  downloads carry no watermark. If a production office later asks for a
  vector file or a specific resolution, check the journal's author
  guidelines; figures can be regenerated in seconds from your saved inputs.
- Fixed-effect or random-effects: which should I report? The forest plot
  tool shows both; the choice depends on whether you assume one common
  effect or a distribution of effects across studies.
- What is the difference between records, reports and studies in PRISMA
  2020? Records are titles/abstracts identified; reports are full-text
  documents retrieved and assessed; studies are the distinct
  investigations, one of which can have several reports.

## Learn the craft

- [Meta, in Practice](https://metainpractice.substack.com): free newsletter
  on systematic reviews and meta-analysis, one practical issue every two
  weeks.
- [Meta分析实操手记](https://wx.zsxq.com/group/15551248281522): paid
  Chinese column covering the whole meta-analysis pipeline, one practical
  instalment each week (early-bird ¥99).
- [Meta-Analysis Template Pack](https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/template-pack.html):
  screening logs, dual-extraction sheets, RoB 2 forms, analysis code and
  submission checklists; now available to buy.

## Notes

- Tools are provided for research use; always verify figures against your
  own analysis before submission.
- Sitemap: https://007-cloud-star.github.io/metaworkbench/sitemap.xml
